replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body:
yeah.. one is using distributed means of distribution / servers hosted in countries with protection against the us kicking in the door. 

The other uses global banking and major distribution platforms that can be sued if they allow the content to exist. They don't even need to sue you... the platform has a responsibility to not allow it.

Ai is a wreaking ball to code ip... its hard to enforce, hard to catch  and no ones cares as much socially. 

But using Goku's face is pretty clear cut. 

You'll get a dmca in about 10 seconds. if you hit any amount of mainstream appeal.   
Private servers for mmos have existed for decades but they generally are underground, keeping a low profile and running their servers in russia and even then they get shutdown constantly.

replies.author: tomato-shadow
replies.body:
That's not how it works lol. Why would everyone just suddenly lose their IP because of AI?

Modding has always existed and it's generally tolerated as long as it's not a) monetized or b) so popular that it actually competes with the original.

There is no such thing as "Making new games with existing ones", that's just modding. And even if people people put out a hundred million mods and try to profit off of them... Those company will just c&d or sue each ones.

But regarding your actual question, that's absolutely not the way forward, no.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: I certainly wouldn't call it "the way forward". The  question you have to ask with any product is, "What am I bringing to the table that existing offerings aren't?" And if you can't answer that question, you will not be successful. You actually have quite a bit going for you with this, as the graphics style is quite pleasing and it's an obvious shoe-in for TFT leveling mechanics with fusions and pseudo-evolutions like Cell/Buu/Frieza/SSJs/etc, and if it was released by someone who actually had IP rights to DBZ you could probably pick up a number of players on that IP. Though if the pokemon tactics game is any indication, not being officially supported and not able to be on major game platforms basically kills its ability to compete from a playerbase perspective (the pokemon tactics game is very well done and maybe has 1/100th the number of players as TFT).
